column1: # `scripts/check-complexity` reports a hit only on a line added or changed since the
# diff base, so these rows matter when a pull request touches one of these lines (a
# reformat, a move) or when the whole tree is audited with `--all`. One row per site:
# `line-hash` is the first 12 hex digits of SHA-256 over the line with runs of
# whitespace collapsed and its ends trimmed: `" ".join(line.split())`. It is a hash of
# the text, not of the line number, so reindenting or moving the site keeps the row
# valid; editing the line's text invalidates it (that edit deserves review). One row
# covers every line in that file with that exact text. In `--all` mode a row that
# matches no hit is an error: delete it when the site is fixed.
# Each row is a pre-existing site the lint cannot distinguish from a real regression
# without types (or a deliberately small, bounded use). The rule is in the reason.
# Do not add rows for new code: fix it, or put `-- complexity: ok (<why>)` on the line
# when the bound is real. See reviews/2026-11-18-complexity-patterns.md (C.1).
